for_editor: Every item sourced only to the EUDA volatile-substances profile (task 79) is not-rechecked: the WebFetch summarizer took the extraction prompt for an instruction embedded in the page and returned a general summary. Under the rules the page was not retried. Items that also cite NIST, the DEA or NIDA were checked against those.
Items confirmed from the EUDA summary (inhalants, poppers, locker room, bolt, hardware, room odouriser, small glass bottles, cyanide antidote) rest on that general summary only.
NIST does not label any of its 'Other names' as a CAS index name; names marked '(CAS index name, NIST)' are confirmed as NIST other names.
NIDA gives three main categories (volatile solvents, gases, aerosols) and calls nitrites 'a special class of inhalants'; names.synonyms[5] says 'four types'.
The cross-reference in members[11].note (nitrous oxide 'covered on its own page') is editorial and was not checked.
Regions for the DEA and NIDA lists are not stated on the pages; they are confirmed as the publisher's jurisdiction.
members[4].note mentions the EUDA table and members[12].note the DEA pages, but neither member lists that page in its source_ids; the editor may want to add them.
